QNX008.title: CPU affinity
QNX008.why: sched_setaffinity / pthread_setaffinity_np and the CPU_* macros have no page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference.
QNX008.qnx_8_0: For the calling thread use ThreadCtl(_NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK, &mask) (also _NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK_GET_AND_SET and _NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK_GET_AND_SET_INHERIT); map CPU numbers to bits of the runmask. The ThreadCtl() page says the runmask commands can only be executed on the calling thread, so code that sets the affinity of ANOTHER thread or process (sched_setaffinity(pid, ...)) has no documented equivalent: the target thread must set its own runmask (verify). sched_getcpu() has no documented equivalent: verify.

QNX009.title: zero-copy transfer (sendfile/splice/tee)
QNX009.why: sendfile, splice, tee and vmsplice have no page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference.
QNX009.qnx_8_0: Fall back to a read()/write() loop (or mmap() of the source file). Keep the Linux path behind an #ifdef and add a portable copy loop. Check your SDP for any BSD-style sendfile() before relying on it (verify).

QNX001.title: epoll event loop
QNX001.why: epoll has no page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference. The ionotify() page states that it 'corresponds to the Linux epoll() function and BSD's kqueue()'.
QNX001.qnx_8_0: Use poll()/ppoll()/select() when you only wait on file descriptors. Use ionotify() with a SIGEV_PULSE event (registered with MsgRegisterEvent()) and receive it with MsgReceivePulse() when the loop must also serve QNX messages, timers or pulses from other threads. ionotify() arms are one-shot: re-arm after every delivery.

QNX007.title: prctl()
QNX007.why: prctl has no page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference.
QNX007.qnx_8_0: PR_SET_NAME / PR_GET_NAME map to pthread_setname_np(0, name) / pthread_getname_np() (documented; the length limit is _NTO_THREAD_NAME_MAX instead of Linux's 16 bytes). Other options (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, PR_SET_DUMPABLE, PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, PR_SET_SECCOMP ...) have no documented single-call equivalent: verify, or use procmgr_ability() for privilege control.

QNX022.title: raw syscall() / SYS_* numbers
QNX022.why: Linux system-call numbers do not exist on QNX; syscall() has no page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference.
QNX022.qnx_8_0: Call the libc/QNX API instead. syscall(SYS_gettid) -> gettid() (documented, <process.h>). Others: find the libc function, or QNX kernel call, that provides the feature.

QNX012.title: sysinfo / load / CPU count helpers
QNX012.why: sys/sysinfo.h, sysinfo(), get_nprocs() and getloadavg() have no page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference.
QNX012.qnx_8_0: sysconf() is documented for configurable limits (page size, open files, ...). For CPU count, memory totals and uptime check which sysconf names your SDP defines and the system page (<sys/syspage.h>); there is no documented load-average call (verify).

QNX013.title: /proc paths (Linux layout)
QNX013.why: QNX has a /proc, but it is a process-manager namespace with its own layout, not Linux text files such as /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/meminfo, /proc/stat or /proc/<pid>/stat.
QNX013.qnx_8_0: Use the QNX /proc interface (devctl() with DCMD_PROC_* commands) described in the Programmer's Guide, sysconf(), or pidin-style queries instead of parsing Linux files. For the executable path, QNX provides /proc/self/exefile (verify on your target).

docs.title: Controlling processes via the /proc filesystem (Programmer's Guide)

QNX014.title: /sys (sysfs) paths
QNX014.why: QNX does not provide Linux sysfs. Paths such as /sys/class/gpio, /sys/class/net or /sys/devices have no QNX counterpart.
QNX014.qnx_8_0: Use the QNX driver/resource-manager interface for the device (GPIO, I2C, SPI, networking APIs, ...). Which one depends on your BSP: verify in the BSP documentation.

QNX030.title: containers, namespaces and seccomp
QNX030.why: clone(CLONE_NEW*), unshare(), setns(), seccomp and cgroups (/sys/fs/cgroup) are Linux kernel features.
QNX030.qnx_8_0: There is no one-to-one mapping. Isolation on QNX is built from process abilities, the security policy and separate process managers/partitions: design the equivalent and verify against the QNX System Security Guide.

QNX104.title: OS detection that only knows Linux
QNX104.why: uname -s / CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME / configure host checks branch on Linux; on a QNX cross build none of the Linux branches apply, and there may be no branch for QNX at all.
QNX104.qnx_8_0: Add a QNX branch (CMake with a QNX toolchain reports CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME = QNX; autoconf host triplets contain 'nto-qnx'): verify with your toolchain and your config.sub version.

QNX023.title: accept4 / dup3 / SOCK_* creation flags
QNX023.why: accept4 and dup3 have no page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference; SOCK_NONBLOCK/SOCK_CLOEXEC support depends on the network stack headers of your SDP.
QNX023.qnx_8_0: Use accept()/dup2()/socket() followed by fcntl(fd, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC) and fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, O_NONBLOCK) (a small wrapper keeps the call sites clean). Note the non-atomic window if you fork concurrently (verify). pipe2() and mkostemp() are documented and can stay.

QNX019.title: Linux/glibc preprocessor guards
QNX019.why: Code under #ifdef __linux__ / __GLIBC__ is not compiled by qcc for QNX, so such branches silently disappear and some #else branches may pick a BSD or generic path that was never tested on QNX.
QNX019.qnx_8_0: Add an explicit __QNXNTO__ (and/or __QNX__) branch, or restructure so the portable code path is the default. qcc predefines the QNX macros: confirm with 'qcc -V... -dM -E - < /dev/null' on your SDP (verify).

QNX034.title: Linux socket options and netlink
QNX034.why: TCP_CORK, TCP_QUICKACK, TCP_USER_TIMEOUT, SO_BINDTODEVICE, MSG_MORE, AF_PACKET and AF_NETLINK are Linux networking features; the QNX networking stack is documented separately from the C Library Reference.
QNX034.qnx_8_0: Check each option in the QNX 8.0 networking documentation / your SDP <netinet/tcp.h>; BSD-style alternatives (for example TCP_NOPUSH for corking, routing sockets instead of netlink) are likely but must be verified.

QNX018.title: Linux-specific ioctl requests
QNX018.why: ioctl request codes such as BLK*, FS_IOC_*, FICLONE, SIOCETHTOOL, EVIOC*, I2C_*/SPI_IOC_* and TUNSETIFF are Linux definitions.
QNX018.qnx_8_0: QNX resource managers are usually controlled with devctl() and DCMD_* commands. Map each request to the corresponding resource-manager command for your driver (verify per driver).

QNX025.title: statfs / sys/vfs.h
QNX025.why: statfs()/fstatfs() and <sys/vfs.h>, <sys/statfs.h> are Linux interfaces (no statfs page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference).
QNX025.qnx_8_0: Use statvfs()/fstatvfs() (documented, <sys/statvfs.h>); map the fields (f_bsize, f_blocks, f_bavail, ...).

QNX005.title: inotify filesystem watches
QNX005.why: QNX 8.0 documents inotify (libfsnotify), but it is served by the fsevmgr filesystem event manager: the program must link -lfsnotify, /dev/fsnotify must exist and be readable, and inotify_init() fails if fsevmgr is not running.
QNX005.qnx_8_0: Keep the inotify code, add -lfsnotify to the link line, make sure fsevmgr runs on the target, and handle inotify_init() failure at start-up. Check event coverage per filesystem on your target (verify). inotify_qnx_ext() enables QNX-specific extensions.

QNX151.title: inotify needs -lfsnotify
QNX151.why: The code uses inotify but no build file links fsnotify.
QNX151.qnx_8_0: Add -lfsnotify to the link line (documented on the inotify_init() page) and ensure fsevmgr runs on the target.

QNX027.title: Linux-only mmap/madvise options
QNX027.why: mmap() on QNX documents MAP_ANON (not MAP_ANONYMOUS), MAP_LAZY, MAP_NORESERVE, MAP_STACK and others; MAP_POPULATE, MAP_HUGETLB, MAP_GROWSDOWN, MAP_LOCKED, MAP_32BIT and mremap() are Linux features.
QNX027.qnx_8_0: Use MAP_ANON, drop prefault/huge-page flags (or find the QNX equivalent in the mmap() page), and replace mremap() with mmap + copy. madvise() has no C Library Reference page: use posix_madvise() (documented) (verify).

QNX026.title: Linux-only clock IDs
QNX026.why: The clock_gettime() page lists CLOCK_REALTIME, CLOCK_MONOTONIC and the CPU-time clocks; CLOCK_BOOTTIME, CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, *_COARSE and CLOCK_TAI are Linux clocks and are not documented for QNX 8.0.
QNX026.qnx_8_0: Use CLOCK_MONOTONIC for intervals and CLOCK_REALTIME for wall time. If you need time-since-boot semantics, decide what to do while suspended (verify behaviour on your target). timer_create() additionally accepts CLOCK_SOFTTIME.

QNX105.title: sanitizers and Linux-only linker flags
QNX105.why: -fsanitize=*, -Wl,--no-undefined and -Wl,-z,* are common on Linux builds; whether your QNX SDP's compiler/linker accepts them is not stated in the pages searched.
QNX105.qnx_8_0: Make them conditional for the QNX target and test the link with your SDP (verify).

QNX020.title: glibc / GNU extensions
QNX020.why: These GNU extensions have no page in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference (they may still be available in your SDP headers or not: the compiler is the judge).
QNX020.qnx_8_0: Provide a small portable replacement in your own code (strchrnul/memrchr/qsort_r/secure_getenv/canonicalize_file_name/get_current_dir_name are a few lines each), or guard the use. Do not assume the glibc behaviour (verify).

limitations: qnxport is a static, pattern-based scan (comments and string literals are understood; no compiler or preprocessor run). It lists the places that need attention and a porting strategy backed by the public QNX 8.0 documentation. It cannot prove that a project builds or behaves correctly on QNX: compile with qcc, run on a QNX 8.0 target and test. Findings marked 'verify' name a likely strategy that could not be confirmed from the public documentation; check them against the headers and docs of your installed QNX SDP. 'Not in the QNX 8.0 C Library Reference' means no page was found for the function, not that the symbol is absent from your SDP.
